question.prompt: Describe a situation where you had to deliver a critical project under a tight deadline. How did you prioritize your work?
expectedPoints: Clear STAR context establishing why the deadline was tight and critical
Systematic scope negotiation and trade-off prioritization (P0 vs P1/P2)
Collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders (Product, QA, Design)
Quantified outcome and reflection on sustainable engineering velocity
commonMistakes: Glorifying heroic overtime / burnout culture rather than smart triage
Cutting corners on testing or security without discussing technical debt

transcript: Candidate: At my previous company, we were preparing for a major customer demo scheduled in three weeks, but our onboarding flow was still unfinished. My task was to lead the frontend delivery for that flow. I audited our backlog with our product manager and realized we had six features queued, which was impossible for a three-week window. I proposed cutting two non-essential customization widgets and postponing automated PDF exports to phase two. This allowed us to focus 100% on the core user sign-up and payment capture steps. I coordinated daily standups with our designer and backend engineer to resolve blocking issues immediately. We completed the core flow two days ahead of the demo, and the client successfully signed the annual contract. In reflection, while we hit the target, our team worked several late nights, so I learned we must identify scope creep earlier during sprint planning.
notes: Good adherence to STAR format. Clear scope cut decisions and cross-functional alignment. Outcome is positive though metrics could be more quantified.
